

library(DBI)
library(odbc)
library(dplyr)

# Open a SINGLE connection block that prompts for MFA just ONCE
con <- dbConnect(odbc::odbc(),
                 Driver   = "ODBC Driver 17 for SQL Server", # Ensure Driver 17 or higher is installed
                 Server   = "YOUR_SERVER_NAME.database.windows.net",
                 Database = "YOUR_DATABASE_NAME",
                 Authentication = "ActiveDirectoryInteractive") # Triggers your interactive MFA prompt

# --- Your MFA prompt (Authenticator App, SMS, etc.) will trigger here ---
# Once approved, this 'con' object remains authenticated for your entire session.


# 1. Download the list of active batch queue IDs using your open connection
batch_indices <- dbGetQuery(con, 
  "SELECT DISTINCT universal_batch_id FROM Production_Batch_Queue ORDER BY universal_batch_id"
)$universal_batch_id

# 2. Pre-stage a local results container 
# This prevents writing back to SQL mid-loop if your server has strict write-policies under MFA
local_results_log <- list()

# next section
for(b_id in batch_indices) {
  
  message(paste("Processing Batch ID:", b_id, "at", Sys.time()))
  
  # Stream data using the open connection (No new login prompt triggered)
  current_batch_data <- dbGetQuery(con, 
    paste("SELECT * FROM Production_Batch_Queue WHERE universal_batch_id =", b_id)
  )
  
  # Extract metadata
  site_name <- current_batch_data$assigned_study_site[1]
  
  # Run the joint model
  model_fit <- tryCatch({
    Jointlcmm(fixed = eGFR ~ observation_time, mixture = ~ observation_time,
              random = ~ observation_time, subject = "patient_id",
              classmb = ~ baseline_bp + baseline_dm + baseline_mental_health * imd_quintile,
              survival = Surv(time, status) ~ mixture(cohort), 
              hazard = "3-quant-splines", hazardtype = "CompetingRisks",
              data = current_batch_data, ng = 3, B = m1)
  }, error = function(e) { NULL })
  
  # Store parameters locally in your list
  if(!is.null(model_fit)) {
    target_idx <- grep("baseline_mental_healthModerate/Severe:imd_quintile1", names(model_fit$best))
    
    local_results_log[[paste0("Batch_", b_id)]] <- data.frame(
      universal_batch_id = b_id,
      assigned_study_site = site_name,
      interaction_log_odds = model_fit$best[target_idx],
      interaction_variance = diag(model_fit$V)[target_idx]
    )
  }
  
  # Critical memory flush
  rm(current_batch_data, model_fit)
  gc()
}



# 1. Combine all individual batch results into one master data frame
final_output_df <- do.call(rbind, local_results_log)

# 2. Write the data to your permanent logging table in a single execution block
dbWriteTable(con, "Meta_Analysis_Output_Log", final_output_df, append = TRUE)

# 3. Disconnect safely
dbDisconnect(con)
